correctness.rationale: With adjacent A=J_(j−1) and B=J_j, the Bessel recurrences cancel the mixed derivative terms and give (r²(A²+B²)²/2)'=(2j−1)r(A⁴−B⁴). The boundary flux is zero at the origin and 2/π² at infinity because the two leading Hankel waves are in quadrature; telescope at a common cutoff. For fixed orders the leading q-th powers have the same periodic mean. The mean-zero primitives are uniformly bounded for 4≤q≤5, giving uniform O(R^−1) tails in the difference, while the mean m(4)=3/8 gives the pole 3/[π²(q−4)]. The power mean-value step gives exactly the stated coefficient with unnormalized arclength; strict ordering persists only over each fixed finite set, and Minkowski gives the matching sharp band-limited bound attained by a first-degree mode. The nonnegative diagonal sum gives the exact log form domain and optimal gap with equality in degrees 0,±1. This does not give an untruncated optimizer or an ordinary extension bound at q=4. Read the frozen VERIFICATION.md and CHECK.py; the recorded finite identities and quadratures are supplementary and the supplied script was not run.
